response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-18
CLINICAL INDICATION: Surveillance. History of treated colon adenocarcinoma. Assess for new pulmonary nodules.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. A. Rahimi (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-05-14
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. No difference in view from prior. Studies are comparable (both reads: yes). Image processing and display contrast differ slightly and the current image has a wider border, which limits judging a subtle density change in the small hilar opacities. A belt and buckle overlie the upper abdomen on the prior only, so the upper abdomen below the diaphragm cannot be compared between studies.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi unremarkable. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, collapse or interstitial pattern. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. No new lung opacity in any zone compared with prior. Small, dense, well-defined rounded opacity at the lateral margin of the left hilum (F1), in the same position with similar shape, density and apparent size on both films. Calcification cannot be confirmed (see CAN'T DETERMINE). Both reads agreed this is stable.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortic knuckle and aortopulmonary window preserved. Hila normal in size and position, with no interval hilar enlargement. Small dense focus projected over the right hilum (F2, F4), present at the same position on both films with similar size and density. Indeterminate: the reads disagreed, as each of F2 and F4 was reported by only one of the two reads. The findings data describe F2 and F4 as the same focus. It may be a vessel seen end-on or a small calcified node.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles sharp. No visible pleural line and no pleural thickening. No effusion or pneumothorax on either study.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly prominent, with a rounded left ventricular contour. Heart borders sharp. Similar size and shape on both PA films (F3). The cardiothoracic ratio was not measured; the radiologist is to measure it in PACS.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture and no destructive bone lesion in the ribs, clavicles, shoulders or visible spine. Bilateral breast shadows overlie the lower zones. No soft tissue gas. Both diaphragm domes well defined, right slightly higher than left, no free gas under the diaphragm. No lines, tubes, ports, pacemaker or surgical clips on either study. External objects only: belt and buckle on the prior, a partly included dense object at the lower image edge on the current.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: None identified. No new pulmonary nodule is seen on the current PA film compared with the prior.
- Unchanged: Small dense left hilar opacity (F1). Small dense right hilar focus (F2, F4), indeterminate as above. Cardiac silhouette size and shape. Mediastinal contour. Both costophrenic angles. Size change is described in words only (similar); no measurements are available. The prior report stated lungs clear with no focal opacity and did not mention the left or right hilar densities, but both are visible on the prior film.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense left hilar opacity a calcified granuloma or node, or a non-calcified nodule? (F1, read A) | Reason: The opacity is small, and a frontal film at this resolution cannot confirm calcification or show its margins in detail. It could also be a vessel end-on. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS and any older films. CT chest if calcification or long-term stability cannot be confirmed.
- Is the small dense right hilar focus a calcified node or a vessel end-on? (F2, read A) | Reason: On a single frontal projection, a small hilar density cannot be separated from a normal vessel seen end-on. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest if clinically relevant.
- Is there a retrocardiac or retrosternal abnormality? (read A) | Reason: Only frontal films were provided. The area behind the heart is seen through the cardiac shadow only. | Recommend: Lateral view if there is clinical concern.
- Is the left perihilar nodule calcified, which would be consistent with a granuloma? (F1, read B) | Reason: The nodule is small and these are downsampled frontal radiographs. Density and internal calcification cannot be confirmed at this resolution. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS and compare with any older studies to establish long-term stability. CT chest if calcification or stability cannot be confirmed.
- Is the small dense focus over the right hilum a vessel end-on, a calcified node or a small nodule? (F4, read B) | Reason: It is a small density superimposed on hilar vessels on a frontal view alone, and the image resolution is limited. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with a lateral view if available. CT chest if it remains unexplained.
- Does the prominent left heart border reflect enlargement of a specific chamber or of the pulmonary artery? (F3, read B) | Reason: A frontal radiograph shows the contour only. It cannot separate the left atrial appendage, the pulmonary artery segment and normal variation. | Recommend: Lateral chest view and clinical correlation. Echocardiography if clinically indicated.
- Is there a retrocardiac or hidden lower lobe abnormality? (read B) | Reason: Only frontal views are provided, and the retrocardiac region is partly obscured by the prominent cardiac silhouette. | Recommend: Lateral view.

IMPRESSION:
1. Small, dense, well-defined rounded opacity at the lateral margin of the left hilum (F1), similar to prior in position, shape, density and apparent size. Calcification cannot be confirmed on this frontal film.
2. Small dense focus over the right hilum (F4, F2), similar to prior. Indeterminate: the reads disagreed, with each reported by only one read. Vessel end-on versus small calcified node cannot be separated on a frontal view.
3. No new pulmonary nodule on the current PA film compared with the prior. Frontal views alone at this resolution cannot exclude small or retrocardiac nodules.
4. Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly prominent, similar to prior (outside the indication). Cardiothoracic ratio to be measured in PACS.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source images in PACS and any older films for F1 and the right hilar focus, and measure the cardiothoracic ratio in PACS.
- CT chest if calcification or long-term stability of the left hilar opacity cannot be confirmed, or if the right hilar focus remains unexplained. No interval is specified in the findings.
- Lateral chest view if there is clinical concern about the retrocardiac or retrosternal region, the lower lobes, or the right hilar focus.
- Echocardiography if clinically indicated for the prominent cardiac contour.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
